$comment: Artifact id -> name tables for artifacts[] / accessories[] in export-schema.json. Static game metadata, not account data: these ids mean the same thing on every account. Published here because the payload carries opaque ints and nothing in it says what they mean - the same reason role-names.json exists. Read live off game build 11.67.0 (RslCompanionExtraction, `BlessingProbe --vaultenums`), and every table records how it was corroborated, because two of them replace tables that were WRONG until 2026-08-02.

kinds.$comment: The SLOT, from the game's IL2CPP `ArtifactKindId` enum. Decides which array a record lands in: 1-6 are gear (artifacts[]), 7-9 accessories (accessories[]). CORRECTION: schemas 7-8 of export-schema.md published a different and incorrect order (1 Weapon, 2 Helmet, 3 Shield, 4 Gauntlets, 5 Chestplate) - a consumer that hard-coded those labels is mislabelling slots. Corroborated independently of the enum by which primary stat each slot always rolls across a 5,780-piece vault: slot 1 is Health on all 411, slot 5 Attack on all 482, slot 6 Defence on all 508, slot 4 Speed on 385 of 508. Those are the game's fixed helmet/weapon/shield/boots primaries.
kinds.source: IL2CPP enum ArtifactKindId + per-slot primary-stat histogram

values.name: Cloak
values.note: The enum calls it Cloak; the UI labels it Amulet.

statKinds.$comment: `primaryBonus.statKindId` and `secondaryBonuses[].statKindId`, from the IL2CPP `StatKindId` enum. NOTE there is no separate id for the percentage form of a stat - one stat kind, and the bonus record's `isAbsolute` says whether its `value` is a flat amount or a fraction. (An older table in the extraction engine encoded 1 Health / 4 Health% / 7 Speed / 8 Critical Rate as distinct ids; that scheme is not what the game uses and was removed.) Corroborated by the same per-slot histogram as `kinds`.

values.name: CriticalHeal
values.note: Declared by the enum; never observed on an artifact (champion-only stat). Ids 1-8 are what artifacts roll.

ranks.$comment: `rankId` - the piece's stars, from the IL2CPP `ArtifactRankId` enum (One..Six). 0 = Unknown is declared but never observed.

rarities.$comment: `rarityId`. WEAKER PROVENANCE than the tables above, stated plainly: no IL2CPP enum was found under any of the names probed (ArtifactRarityId, ArtifactRarity, RarityId, Rarity, ItemRarityId), so these are the uploader's long-standing labels, supported only by the observed value range (1-6 across 5,780 pieces) matching the game's six quality tiers in order. Treat the ids as authoritative and the names as a convenience.

sets.$comment: `setKindId`. 0 means NO SET - a real value, not 'unknown'. PROVENANCE: these names are the uploader's table, corroborated against the live vault by their gap pattern - the ids this table skips (42, 55, 56) are exactly the ids absent from 5,780 real artifacts, which a fabricated list would not reproduce. It is NOT derived from the game's `ArtifactSetKindId` enum: that enum's 72 members carry explicit values rather than running 0..71 (its five accessory sets are 1000-1004), so reading the Nth member as id N mislabels everything from id 4 onward - a trap worth stating, because the enum is otherwise the obvious source. The five accessory sets 1000-1004 are OBSERVED in live data but NOT NAMED here for that reason. Authoritative set metadata (names, bonuses, piece counts, including 1000-1004) belongs in the RslCompanionMetadata artifact-set catalog, joined on this id; this table is a convenience for the common sets.
sets.source: uploader table; gap-pattern corroborated against 5,780 live artifacts
